jail.finding: The message asks for $2,000 in gift cards. Real jails, courts, and lawyers never ask for gift cards. Gift cards are a favorite of scammers because the money is hard to get back.
It says "don't tell mom." Asking you to keep it secret is a trick to stop you from checking with family, who would spot the scam.
This matches the well-known "grandparent scam" word for word: a grandchild in jail, urgent need for money, and secrecy. The FTC (the U.S. consumer protection agency) warns about this exact story.
The sender never says their name. "It's me" lets the scammer get you to guess a grandchild's name for them.
There are no links or phone numbers in the message, so there were none to check.

verdict.headline: This is a scam. Do not buy any gift cards or send money.
reasons: It asks for $2,000 in gift cards. Real jails and lawyers never ask for gift cards.
It tells you to keep it secret from Mom, so you won't check with family.
This is the well-known "grandparent scam" that the FTC warns about.
nextSteps: Do not reply and do not buy any gift cards.
Call your grandchild on the phone number you already have for them, or call their mom or dad.

alert.summary: Grandma got a "grandparent scam" message: someone pretending to be a grandchild said they were in jail, asked for $2,000 in gift cards, and said "don't tell mom." She has already sent one $500 gift card.
alert.suggestedAction: Please call her now. Help her call the gift card company (number on the card's back) to freeze the funds, make sure she sends nothing more, and help file reports at reportfraud.ftc.gov.

steps.title: Call the gift card company right now
steps.detail: Turn the gift card or its receipt over and find the customer service number printed there, or go to the company's official website. Tell them you were scammed and ask them to freeze the money on the card. The sooner you call, the better the chance to save it.

steps.title: Keep the card and the receipt
steps.detail: Do not throw anything away. The card number and the store receipt are what the company and police need to track the money.

steps.title: Do not send any more gift cards
steps.detail: The scammer may call or write again and ask for more money, or say there is a new problem. Do not reply and do not send anything else.

steps.title: Call your grandchild on the number you already have
steps.detail: Use the phone number you saved for them before, not any number from this message. You can also call their mom or dad. It is fine to tell them. Scammers say "don't tell mom" because family would catch the trick.

steps.title: Report it to the FTC
steps.detail: Go to reportfraud.ftc.gov and fill out the short form. You can paste the report below. This helps stop these scammers.

steps.title: Report it to the FBI
steps.detail: Go to ic3.gov and file a report. You can paste the report below.

steps.title: Save the message
steps.detail: Do not delete the message. Take a picture or screenshot of it, and write down the phone number or account it came from.
